chunks: From al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, he said:
I heard Abū ‘Abd Allāh (peace be upon him) saying: 'The devils are more numerous upon the believer than wasps upon meat.'

key_terms.الزَّنَابِيرِ: Wasps (a type of stinging insect, used here to signify numerous and persistent attackers)
key_terms.الشَّيَاطِينَ: Devils (plural of shayṭān, meaning jinn or demons who misguide humans)

ai.seo_question: What is the analogy used in Shia hadith to describe the frequency of devils' attacks on a believer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) uses a vivid analogy to illustrate the intensity of spiritual struggle for a believer. Just as wasps are constantly attracted to and swarm around a piece of meat, devils are persistently and numerous in their efforts to misguide and afflict the believer.
